{
 "version": "20261027-premiere",
 "note": "Two layers. 'studies': one PREMIERE-format line per cited PMID (arms or design, main result, limitation), curated from the team's own evidence-summary PPT text (V15 libraries) and the site's verified text; 'quotes' are the exact source passages that contain every number. 'options': per treatment option (key = page slug + hash of the option's visible statement), the numerical results that the option's own text reports and attributes to a named cited study, restated in LRT style. Only these option rows display numbers under an option; a shared citation alone never brings a number into an option. 'reference_groups' and 'reference_links': explicit, reviewed presentation of source-study evidence from the HCC treatment references (liver-directed reference, systemic matrix, HCC roadmap text and critique records) for the linked modality or regimen, with the studied population, treatment arms and endpoint/horizon; every number is guarded against that study's verified site text or an exact quoted passage. Not an eligibility rule and not a regrading.",
 "studies": {
  "1309988": {
   "label": "Bismuth-Corlette",
   "design": "Case series",
   "arms": "Case series · 23 resections",
   "result": "Type sets operation (I excision; II +caudate; III +hepatectomy; IV LT); 3-y survival 50% clear vs 12% microscopic-residual margins, untested",
   "caution": "23 resections over thirty years at one centre; no comparison group or statistical test",
   "quotes": [
    "It rests on 23 resections over thirty years at one centre",
    "Group C (clear margins, n=9): survival 100%, 71% and 50% at 1, 2 and 3 years. Group B (microscopic residual, n=10): 82%, 43% and 12%"
   ]
  },
  "1738990": {
   "label": "Jones 1992",
   "design": "Retrospective cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective cohort · 1454 outpatient CTs",
   "result": "Hepatic lesions ≤15 mm on 17% of outpatient CTs: 51% benign, 22% malignant, 27% unclassifiable; solitary lesion malignant in 5% of cancer patients",
   "caution": "82% had known cancer (surveillance, not incidental, population); benignity mostly by CT stability",
   "quotes": [
    "1454 consecutive outpatient CT examinations; 254 patients (17%) with lesions <=15 mm",
    "Of the 254, 129 (51%) judged benign, 55 (22%) malignant, 70 (27%) unclassifiable",
    "with one small lesion 65% probably benign and only 4/86 (5%) malignant",
    "82% of patients with small lesions (209/254) had a known extrahepatic malignancy"
   ]
  },
  "2571019": {
   "label": "Spigelman 1989",
   "design": "Prospective cohort",
   "arms": "Prospective screening cohort · 102 FAP patients",
   "result": "Duodenal abnormality in 100 of 102 FAP patients; papilla adenomatous twice as often as peripapillary area (81% vs 41%); stage IV in 11%",
   "caution": "Cross-sectional, no cancer outcomes; Spigelman stage never validated and omits the papilla",
   "quotes": [
    "102 patients screened prospectively",
    "100 of 102 patients had duodenal abnormalities",
    "the papilla itself was twice as likely to be adenomatous as the peripapillary area (81% vs 41%)",
    "11 of 102 (11%) had stage IV"
   ]
  },
  "3950039": {
   "label": "Karhunen 1986",
   "design": "Case series",
   "arms": "Autopsy case series · 95 men aged 35-69",
   "result": "Benign liver lesion in 49/95 (52%), mostly bile duct tumours (27%, mean 1.3 mm) and cavernous haemangiomas (20%, mean 5.2 mm)",
   "caution": "Forensic autopsies of Finnish men only; millimetre-scale lesions invisible on imaging",
   "quotes": [
    "95 consecutive medicolegal autopsies, all men aged 35-69",
    "Tumours or tumour-like conditions in 49/95 (52%)",
    "Bile duct tumours (microhamartomas plus adenomas, grouped together) 26/95 (27%), mean size 1.3 mm",
    "Cavernous haemangioma 19/95 (20%), mean size 5.2 mm"
   ]
  },
  "8594428": {
   "label": "Milan criteria",
   "design": "Cohort",
   "arms": "Single-centre prospective cohort · 48 transplanted patients",
   "result": "Single HCC ≤5 cm or up to three nodules ≤3 cm: four-year OS 75%, RFS 83%; within limits on explant 85% vs 50% beyond (P<0.01)",
   "caution": "Limits applied to explant pathology in the same 48 patients; only four recurrences; survival from LT",
   "quotes": [
    "48 patients with cirrhosis and unresectable early-stage HCC transplanted",
    "Actuarial four-year overall survival was 75 percent and four-year recurrence-free survival 83 percent",
    "four-year survival was 85 percent and recurrence-free survival 92 percent, versus 50 percent and 59 percent in the 13 (27 percent) whose tumours exceeded the limits (P<0.01 for survival",
    "a single HCC of 5 cm or less, or up to three nodules each 3 cm or less"
   ]
  },
  "8831597": {
   "label": "Bruix 1996",
   "design": "Prospective cohort",
   "arms": "HVPG ≥10 vs <10 mmHg · prospective cohort, 29 resected patients",
   "result": "Unresolved decompensation at 3 months in 11/15 vs 0/14 (P<0.0002); HVPG only independent predictor (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.12-3.22)",
   "caution": "Single-centre; 11 events vs 44 candidate variables; cut-off not derived; endpoint mostly ascites; no survival",
   "quotes": [
    "Unresolved decompensation developed in 11 of the 15 patients with an HVPG of 10 mmHg or more but in none of the 14 patients with an HVPG below 10 mmHg (P<0.0002).",
    "HVPG was the only independent predictor on logistic regression (odds ratio 1.90; 95% CI 1.12 to 3.22; P<0.0001)",
    "The separation is complete, 11 of 15 against 0 of 14, in a cohort of 29 patients with 11 events screened against 44 candidate variables.",
    "11 developed unresolved hepatic decompensation at 3 months"
   ]
  },
  "9885589": {
   "label": "Schwartz 1999",
   "design": "Retrospective cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective cohort · 2978 cancer patients",
   "result": "Sub-centimetre hepatic lesions reported in 12.7%; 80.2% stable (benign), 11.6% metastatic, up to 19.8% if indeterminates counted malignant",
   "caution": "Report-based, no histology; benignity by CT stability; known-cancer tertiary patients only",
   "quotes": [
    "Small hepatic lesions reported in 378/2978 (12.7%) patients",
    "Classified benign (stable >=6 months) in 303/378 (80.2%), metastatic (interval growth) in 44/378 (11.6%)",
    "up to 19.8% if indeterminates are counted as malignant"
   ]
  },
  "10493478": {
   "label": "Fong CRS",
   "design": "Cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective cohort · 1001 patients",
   "result": "CRLM resection: 5-y OS 37%, 10-y OS 22%, 30-day mortality 2.8%; Clinical Risk Score 5-y OS 60% at score 0 vs 14% at score 5 (p<0.0001)",
   "caution": "Score derived and assessed in the same 1001 patients, no validation; end strata n=52 and n=14; not monotonic",
   "quotes": [
    "5-year survival 37% and 10-year survival 22%",
    "Surgical (30-day) mortality 2.8%",
    "was highly predictive (p<0.0001): 5-year survival 60% at score 0 (n=52) down to 14% at score 5 (n=14)",
    "The score was derived and assessed in the same 1001 patients with no split sample"
   ]
  },
  "10615075": {
   "label": "Kemeny adjuvant HAI",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "HAI floxuridine + systemic FU vs systemic FU alone",
   "result": "Primary two-year OS 86% vs 72% (P=0.03, landmark) but whole KM curves NS (p=0.21); two-year hepatic PFS 90% vs 60% (P<0.001)",
   "caution": "Only 26% got more than half the planned floxuridine; 6 of 74 never received HAI; single centre",
   "quotes": [
    "Two-year actuarial overall survival was 86% with combined therapy versus 72% with systemic therapy alone (P=0.03)",
    "the Kaplan-Meier comparison gives p=0.21",
    "Two-year survival free of hepatic progression was 90% versus 60% (P<0.001)",
    "Only 26% of combined-therapy patients received more than half the planned floxuridine, 6 of 74 never received any hepatic arterial infusion at all"
   ]
  },
  "11932907": {
   "label": "Jarnagin 2002",
   "design": "Retrospective cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective cohort · 27 patients",
   "result": "Resected combined HCC-CC: 5-year overall survival 24%; no patient had underlying cirrhosis (0%); single-institution surgical series",
   "caution": "Small single-centre series, evolving pathology criteria; predates Brunt 2018 and WHO 2019 definitions",
   "quotes": [
    "27 patients with combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma",
    "5-year overall survival 24% after resection of combined HCC-CC",
    "No patient in the cohort had underlying cirrhosis (0%)",
    "Predates the Brunt 2018 consensus and the 2019 WHO classification entirely"
   ]
  },
  "11981766": {
   "label": "Lo · Hong Kong TACE RCT",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "Single-centre RCT · 80 unresectable HCC: TACE vs symptomatic care",
   "result": "Chemoembolisation improved survival over symptomatic treatment; no clear benefit in tumours over 5 cm or with unilobar portal vein obstruction",
   "caution": "Subgroups underpowered; selected Asian, mostly hepatitis B, population",
   "quotes": [
    "OS ↑ vs supportive",
    "80 of 279 Asian patients with newly diagnosed unresectable HCC",
    "No demonstrable benefit in tumours larger than 5 cm or in patients with unilobar portal vein obstruction",
    "Loss of statistical power after stratification"
   ]
  },
  "12049862": {
   "label": "Llovet · Barcelona TACE RCT",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "Three-arm RCT · 112 unresectable HCC: TAE, TACE or symptomatic care",
   "result": "Chemoembolisation prolonged survival over symptomatic treatment (OS HR 0.47)",
   "caution": "Strict selection: 112 of 903 registered patients randomised",
   "quotes": [
    "OS HR 0.47 vs supportive",
    "112 of 903 registered patients with unresectable HCC",
    "Sequential three-arm randomised controlled trial"
   ]
  },
  "15042359": {
   "label": "Surveillance RCT",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "6-monthly AFP + ultrasound screening vs no screening (cluster RCT)",
   "result": "HCC mortality 83.2 vs 131.5 per 100,000 over five years (rate ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.98), a 37% reduction",

   "quotes": [

    "giving HCC mortality of 83.2 versus 131.5 per 100,000 and a mortality rate ratio of 0.63 (95% CI 0.41-0.98), a 37% reduction",
    "the 83.2 against 131.5 per 100,000 five-year rates",
    "Compliance with screening was only 58.2 percent"
   ]
  },
  "15131794": {
   "label": "Cooperative cyst study",
   "design": "Prospective cohort",
   "arms": "Diagnostic accuracy · 112 of 341 patients",
   "result": "Cyst fluid CEA cut-off 192 ng/mL for mucinous cyst: sensitivity 75.0%, specificity 83.6%, accuracy 79.2%; beat EUS morphology (50.9%) and cytology (58.7%)",
   "caution": "Cut-off derived and tested in same patients; only 112 of 341 (33%) had histology (verification bias)",
   "quotes": [
    "341 consecutive patients enrolled and underwent EUS-FNA; 112 with histological confirmation analysed",
    "CEA at the optimal cutoff of 192 ng/mL: sensitivity 75.0% (42/56), specificity 83.6% (46/55), accuracy 79.2% (88/111)",
    "accuracy 50.9% (57/112)\nCytology: sensitivity 34.5% (19/55), specificity 83.3% (45/54), accuracy 58.7% (64/109)",
    "Only 112 of 341 enrolled patients (33%) had histological verification"
   ]
  },
  "15997444": {
   "label": "Jones 2005 CRLM biopsy",
   "design": "Retrospective cohort",
   "arms": "Biopsied vs not biopsied before referral · retrospective, 598 patients",
   "result": "4-y OS 32.5% vs 46.7% (log rank p=0.008); needle-track deposits in 19% of biopsied; benign disease resected in 1.2% without biopsy",
   "caution": "Not randomised; biopsied had 61% vs 26% synchronous disease; adjusted effect reported without HR or CI",
   "quotes": [
    "Four-year overall survival 32.5% (s.e. 5.5) in the biopsied group vs 46.7% (s.e. 2.8) in the non-biopsied group, p=0.008 by log rank",
    "In 598 patients resected for colorectal liver metastases at one specialist centre, those biopsied before referral had needle-track deposits in 19% and a 14% lower 4-year survival",
    "inadvertent resection of benign disease is rare (1.2%)",
    "61% of the biopsied patients had synchronous disease against 26% of the others"
   ]
  },
  "16111953": {
   "label": "Harewood 2005",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "Prophylactic pancreatic stent vs no stent",
   "result": "Pancreatitis within 24 h after snare ampullectomy 0% (0/10) vs 33% (3/9), p = 0.02; stopped early at interim; ITT 9% vs 25%, p = 0.3 (not significant)",
   "caution": "Only 19 patients, single centre and endoscopist; stopped early; significance lost on intention-to-treat",
   "quotes": [
    "Post-procedure pancreatitis occurred in 3 of 19 patients within 24 hours",
    "33% (3/9) versus 0% (0/10), p = 0.02",
    "gave 25% versus 9% with statistical significance lost, p = 0.3"
   ]
  },
  "16111956": {
   "label": "Pooled fluid analysis",
   "design": "Pooled analysis",
   "arms": "Pooled individual-patient analysis · 12 studies, 450 patients",
   "result": "CEA >800 ng/mL for mucinous: sensitivity 48%, specificity 98%; CEA <5 ng/mL for SCA/pseudocyst: 50%, 95%; cytology sensitivity for malignancy 48%",
   "caution": "Cutoffs fitted in the same pooled data (no validation); IPMN excluded; per-marker denominators far below 450",
   "quotes": [
    "12 studies, 450 patients",
    "CEA >800 ng/mL identified MCA or MCAC: sensitivity 48%, specificity 98%",
    "CEA <5 ng/mL identified SCA or pseudocyst: sensitivity 50%, specificity 95%",
    "Cytology showed malignant cells in 53 of 111 MCAC (48%)"
   ]
  },
  "16134179": {
   "label": "Gupta embolisation",
   "design": "Cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective · HAE (bland) vs HACE (chemoembolisation)",
   "result": "Carcinoid: response 81.0% vs 44.4% (OR 6.41, P=0.002), no PFS or OS difference; islet cell: response 25% vs 50% (P=0.06, not significant)",

   "quotes": [

    "In islet cell carcinoma HACE trended better than HAE for response (50% vs 25%, P = 0.06)",
    "Neither grade nor Ki-67 is reported anywhere."
   ]
  },
  "16135931": {
   "label": "Rea 2005",
   "design": "Cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective: neoadjuvant chemoradiation + LT vs resection",
   "result": "5-y survival 82% after LT (n=38, from transplant) vs 21% after resection (n=26), p=0.022; 58% at 5 y from enrolment for all 71",

    "33 of the 71 protocol patients never reached transplant"
   ]
  },
  "16327281": {
   "label": "Sendai 2006",
   "design": "Consensus",
   "arms": "Consensus statement · IAP working group",
   "result": "Resect all main-duct/mixed IPMN and all MCN; observe asymptomatic branch-duct IPMN; resect on symptoms, nodules, cyst >30 mm or duct >6 mm",
   "caution": "No cohort or evidence grading; malignancy rates are prevalences in small resected series",

   ]
  },
  "16432361": {
   "label": "Triponez 2006",
   "design": "Registry cohort",
   "arms": "Registry cohort · 108 MEN1 patients",
   "result": "MEN1 NF-pNET metastasis rose with size, 4% at ≤10 mm to 43% >30 mm (basis for no surgery <20 mm); curative surgery vs none: no survival difference",

    "the basis for not operating below 20 mm, although that specific threshold rests on single-digit event counts, imaging-defined metastasis and 4 years of follow-up",
    "survival curves for curative surgery and no surgery did not differ significantly"
   ]
  },
  "16495695": {
   "label": "Chen RCT",
   "design": "RCT",
   "arms": "Percutaneous ablation vs resection (solitary HCC ≤5 cm)",
   "result": "ITT 4-yr OS 65.9% vs 64.0% and DFS 48.2% vs 51.6%; no significant difference (no HR reported)",

    "Post-randomisation exclusion occurred in 19 of 90 patients assigned to ablation",
    "solitary HCC of 5 cm or less, Child-Pugh A liver function"
   ]
  },
  "16496320": {

   "design": "Retrospective cohort",
   "arms": "Retrospective cohort · 96 resected adenomas",

    "HCC or borderline HCA/HCC in 46% of beta-catenin-activated tumours, never in inflammatory lesions and rarely in HNF1A-mutated (P=0.004)",
    "Mean tumour diameter was 74-81 mm across every group"

  },

    "bilirubin above 3 mg/dL in 18.6% versus 0% (P = .006)"
   ]
  },

It does not show that ablation changes the course of the disease: 80% of imaged patients developed new or progressive liver disease",

  "18008357": {

   "arms": "ELTR registry · 59 LT recipients for HEHE",

  },
  "18358928": {
   "label": "EORTC 40983",
   "design": "RCT",

      "design": "RCT",

      "result": "Primary endpoint met: median PFS not reached vs 18.0 mo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73); 24-mo PFS 65.1% vs 33.0%; no OS or QoL difference",

      "quotes": [
        "204 patients with unresectable or metastatic, somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 (Ki-67 under 10%) non-functioning enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours randomised at 48 centres in 14 countries between June 2006 and April 2013: 101 to lanreotide Autogel 120 mg and 103 to placebo, with 96% having had no documented progression in the preceding 3 to 6 months.",
        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 and 65% versus 33% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "Every subgroup estimate rests on a handful of events. The trial recorded 92 progression events in all, so the midgut (0.35), pancreas (0.45) and high-hepatic-volume (0.45, CI 0.22 to 0.91) hazard ratios each come from fewer than 30 events, and no interaction test is reported for any of them.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lanreotide within the 96-week fixed study duration, so the delay is known only to exceed the observation window, and the 96-week design cannot address how long treatment should continue.",
        "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression. That is a restatement of the trial's design, not an answer to the question of whether delaying treatment costs the patient anything.",
        "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance. Cholelithiasis occurred in 10% against 3% and hyperglycaemia in 5% against 0%, and the serious treatment-related events in the lanreotide arm include biliary fistula and cholelithiasis, in patients who may later need hepatectomy or arterial therapy; the discussion calls the safety profile favourable by comparison with targeted agents and chemotherapy.",
        "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here."

{
 "about": "One-line summaries for evidence-library sources that have no PubMed study line: guidelines, policy, review guidance, registry records, abstracts and local documents. Ids: roadmap:<slug>:<nonpm key> and transplant:<source key>. Each says what the source is and what the page uses it for (at most 160 characters); every number in a line occurs in the source's own citation, note or locator or in the page's own text (tools/test_source_summaries.py). PubMed papers use their compact study line (tools/compact_evidence_source.json). Written 30 October 2026 by Analyst B (Claude.ai) for Hao Liu.",
 "summaries": {
  "roadmap:adenoma:generevgsd": "GeneReviews entry for glycogen storage disease type I; supplies that condition's imaging intervals in the page's surveillance-by-source table.",

  "roadmap:adenoma:optn": "Allocation policy; cited for adenoma not being a standardized MELD exception and for the extension cycle, as stated in the local protocol, not re-verified.",
  "roadmap:adenoma:optnnlrb": "Review-board guidance, not policy; basis for considering specified high-risk, unresectable or syndromic adenoma at a recommended MMaT-3, nothing automatic.",
  "roadmap:adenoma:recist": "Solid-tumour response criteria; cited only as the source of EASL's 20% diameter growth trigger, which has never been validated in benign liver lesions.",
  "roadmap:adenoma:uthprotocol": "Local UTHealth draft protocol (V3), not final policy; the sole authority for this page's transplant assessment and routes, with VERIFY items still open.",
  "roadmap:adenoma:who2019": "WHO tumour classification; the adenoma subtype and uncertain-malignant-potential nomenclature used by the male adenoma series this page cites.",
  "roadmap:ampullary:ajcc8": "Staging manual; the page's ampulla of Vater TNM, stage groups and grade, taken as reproduced in the NCCN ampullary guideline.",
  "roadmap:ampullary:cap": "Pathology reporting protocol; source of the 1 mm positive-margin definition and the minimum data set NCCN abbreviates; PERIPAN's template is the alternative.",

  "roadmap:ampullary:nccnpanc": "US national guideline for pancreatic cancer; used for the margin, specimen-inking and lymphadenectomy questions ampullary surgery shares with it.",
  "roadmap:ampullary:periwork": "PERIPAN consensus supplement; only its summary tables were used for this draft, and the full document must be read before the page is ratified.",
  "roadmap:ampullary:who5": "WHO tumour classification; the subtype framework PERIPAN refines, consulted through PERIPAN rather than read directly for this draft.",
  "roadmap:chcca:ajcc8": "Staging manual; the page stages combined tumours with the intrahepatic bile duct system, using the tables as reproduced in NCCN Biliary v1.2026.",

    "roadmap:nelm:optn-nlrb": "Review-board guidance, not policy; sets the nonstandard MMaT-3 NELM route and imaging-timing rules, and states no age or hepatic-burden cutoff.",
    "roadmap:nelm:optn9": "Allocation policy; cited because NELM is not a standardized exception, and for the MMaT score floor under Policy 9.4.E and 90-day extensions.",
    "roadmap:pcyst:euro2013": "Superseded 2013 European consensus; listed because NCCN cites it, so a reader following NCCN reaches thresholds the 2018 guideline replaced.",
    "roadmap:pcyst:kyotopdf": "Full text of the Kyoto 2024 IPMN guidelines, read in full; the page's high-risk and worrisome features, surveillance, discontinuation and remnant rules.",
    "roadmap:pcyst:nccn": "US national guideline with no cyst algorithm; cited for its summary of Kyoto and a superseded European statement, and for its IPMN and MCN resection rules.",
    "roadmap:pcyst:who2019": "WHO tumour classification; the cyst entity definitions and two-tier dysplasia grading this page uses, not re-verified against the current online edition.",
    "roadmap:pdac:a021806": "Registry record of a phase III of perioperative versus adjuvant chemotherapy, active and not recruiting; no results posted, cited only as an open question.",
    "roadmap:pdac:cap": "Pathology protocol, cited through NCCN for the 1 mm positive-margin rule and millimetre clearance reporting; current version still to be confirmed.",
    "roadmap:pdac:conko004": "Randomised enoxaparin trial via NCCN text only: fewer symptomatic VTE, no survival effect, so NCCN does not recommend routine LMWH prophylaxis.",
    "roadmap:pdac:doc-fda-daraxonrasib": "FDA approval announcement (August 2026); cited for the US indication in metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after at least one prior systemic treatment.",
    "roadmap:pdac:espac3": "Secondary ESPAC-3 analysis via NCCN text only: completing adjuvant chemotherapy, not start time, predicted survival; open to obvious confounding.",
    "roadmap:pdac:isgps": "ISGPS consensus statement read from the abstract only; source of the standard lymphadenectomy definition, so the surgery item it supports is graded C.",
    "roadmap:pdac:nccn": "US national guideline (unversioned extraction); the page's workup, resectability, neoadjuvant, pathology, systemic, radiation and supportive-care source.",
    "roadmap:pdac:paxg": "Randomised phase 3 of PAXG versus mFOLFIRINOX, via NCCN text only: longer event-free survival; NCCN lists it as useful in certain circumstances.",
    "roadmap:pdac:rtog0848": "Randomised adjuvant chemoradiation trial, via NCCN text only: benefit in node-negative, none in node-positive patients; primary paper not read.",
    "roadmap:pnet:firstdraft": "Page statement, not a source: no MH roadmap or alignment worksheet exists for PNET, so nothing here is an institutional decision.",
    "roadmap:pnet:fulltext": "Page method note: 28 of 33 papers read in full and abstracted; names the guidance still cited from programme copies or abstracts only.",
    "roadmap:pnet:nccn": "US national guideline (unversioned extraction); the page's diagnosis, functioning and nonfunctioning tumour, pathology, surgery, systemic and MEN1 content.",
    "roadmap:pnet:nct05040360": "Registry record of an ongoing randomised trial of chemotherapy after PNET resection; the destination for patients wanting adjuvant therapy, not for results.",
    "roadmap:pnet:nelm": "Local MH NELM roadmap (draft v0.6) as rendered on its pathway page; the destination for any patient here who develops or presents with liver metastases.",
    "roadmap:pnet:who2019": "WHO digestive tumour classification; the NET grading criteria on this page, taken from the table NCCN reproduces with permission.",
    "transplant:H-policy": "Allocation policy (OPTN 9.5.I): the standardized HCC exception's Class 5 burden, AFP and imaging rules applied here; it sets eligibility, not best treatment.",
    "transplant:I-focality": "Pathology protocol (CAP v4.3.0.0); its AJCC8 pT and focality definitions set how confirmed satellite and other iCCA nodules are counted at selection.",
    "transplant:I-satellites": "Structured reporting standard (RCPA); cited for the point that iCCA has no clear universal satellite definition when nodules are counted.",
    "transplant:N-crlm": "Review-board guidance, not policy; CRLM steps follow it as nonstandard review, not automatic; its >10% progression footnote differs from usual RECIST 1.1.",
    "transplant:N-hca": "Review-board guidance, not policy, for hepatic adenoma; its alternative review routes structure the exception-route, review and follow-up steps.",
    "transplant:N-hcc": "Review-board guidance for HCC, not policy; used for contraindications, beyond-criteria downstaging, imaging timing and individual exception review.",
    "transplant:N-hehe": "Review-board guidance, not policy, for hepatic epithelioid hemangioendothelioma; used at each step from diagnosis and staging to submission.",
    "transplant:N-icca": "Review-board guidance, not policy, for iCCA and mixed HCC-iCCA; the basis of each step from histology and selection to stability and the exception request.",
    "transplant:N-net": "Review-board guidance, not policy, for NET liver metastases; the basis of each step from grade and primary treatment to disease control and renewal.",
    "transplant:NCCN-crlm": "US national guideline (Colon v2.2026, COL-D); cited for continuing colorectal cancer care and supportive care when transplant is unsuitable.",
    "transplant:NCCN-hcc": "US national guideline (HCC v2.2026); cited for treatment reassessment and local, systemic, resection and supportive options when the transplant plan changes.",
    "transplant:NCCN-icca": "US national guideline (Biliary v1.2026, INTRA-1); cited for iCCA treatment and supportive care when transplant criteria are not met.",
    "transplant:NCCN-net": "US national guideline (NET v1.2026); cited for continuing NET treatment and symptom-focused supportive care when transplant is unsuitable.",
    "transplant:NCCN-pcca": "US national guideline (Biliary v1.2026, EXTRA-1); cited for treatment and supportive care when the pCCA transplant protocol is unsuitable.",
    "transplant:NCI-support": "NCI fact sheet on palliative care in cancer; supports each pathway's best supportive care plan and that palliative care can accompany treatment.",
    "transplant:P-policy": "Allocation policy (OPTN 9.5.A): the hilar CCA exception (approved center protocol, neoadjuvant therapy, operative staging, mass <3 cm) applied at each step.",
    "transplant:crlm_seca3": "Registry record of the Oslo SECA-III randomized trial; cited only for its eligibility wording on prior extrahepatic disease; recruiting, no results posted.",
    "transplant:doc:avastin-label": "US prescribing information for bevacizumab; its 28-day holds before elective and after major surgery are a label minimum, not a proven safe interval before LT.",
    "transplant:doc:lirads-rt-tra": "ACR LI-RADS radiation treatment response algorithm (2024): stable or decreasing enhancement after radiation can be nonprogressing, not failure to retreat.",
    "transplant:doc:zortress-label": "US prescribing information for everolimus; adult liver-transplant use must not start before postoperative day 30; the label describes hepatic-artery thrombosis.",
    "transplant:hhs_irb": "US federal regulation (45 CFR 46.111) setting the criteria for IRB approval; cited so a proposed high-risk transplant study opens only with research approval.",
    "transplant:nlrb": "Review-board guidance, not policy; the high-risk reviews quote its diagnosis-specific criteria as nonbinding allocation guidance, with no outcome data.",
    "transplant:optn": "Binding OPTN policy (allocation and living donation); the high-risk reviews cite it to keep allocation, donor protection and reporting duties separate.",
    "transplant:optn_ethics": "OPTN Ethics Committee principles for organ allocation; cited for judging a high-risk indication by pathway-level benefit and the opportunity cost to others."
  }
}

Oncology portal · Interactive LRT matrix · pCCA roadmap

Liver-directed therapy · perihilar cholangiocarcinoma

What changed in the pCCA pathway

Evidence review updated 23 October 2026

Working draft for multidisciplinary discussion. Not ratified institutional clinical policy.

  • Before transplant: OPTN requires an approved neoadjuvant protocol and operative staging but does not mandate a particular radiation technique. Regimen selection remains a program decision.
  • Outside transplant: NCCN lists chemoradiation without requiring prior systemic control. BSG supports selected SBRT/PBT after systemic therapy. A routine survival advantage remains unproven.
  • After resection: NCCN lists chemoradiation for R1 margins or positive nodes and as a nonpreferred R0/node-negative option. Systemic therapy and clinical trials are preferred.
  • Different thresholds: NCCN clinical LT consideration uses ≤3 cm; OPTN allocation requires a single mass <3 cm when present. Source: NCCN v1.2026, original PDF pages 23–24; OPTN 9.5.A.
  • Biliary interventions: Recent RFA trials did not demonstrate routine survival or patency benefit. PDT is not recommended outside trials. I-125 stent results do not establish HAIC efficacy or transplant bridging.

Added evidence

  • Welling, Liver Transplantation 2014: 12 RT-treated patients, 11 receiving SBRT, six transplanted.
  • Soliman, Transplantation Direct 2025: chemotherapy-only versus RT-containing protocols; no significant difference, not proof of equivalence.
  • Hoogwater, BJS Open 2023: lower recurrence hazard but more vascular complications with neoadjuvant chemoradiation; no significant OS difference.
  • ABC-07 planning QA, STRONG II protocol, and STRONG II benchmark QA: planning and research context, not new efficacy results.

Updated chart

Open the decision-chart PDF · Full evidence-matrix PDF

ABCDE review: A Codex; B Claude.ai; C Claude.science; D Doximity; E OpenEvidence. Recommendations were reconciled against sources; reviewer agreement is not clinical approval.

pCCA liver-directed treatment evidence

Evidence reconciled 2 November 2026

Working draft for multidisciplinary discussion. Not ratified institutional clinical policy.

  • Before transplant: OPTN requires an approved neoadjuvant protocol and operative staging but does not mandate a particular radiation technique. Regimen selection remains a program decision.
  • Outside transplant: NCCN lists chemoradiation without requiring prior systemic control. BSG supports selected SBRT/PBT after systemic therapy. A routine survival advantage remains unproven.

Added evidence
